Maintenance Report — MNT-0004-003

Asset: WELL-0004 (SW-23 Well 004, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 21 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 21 Apr 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0004-0026 on 2023-04-20 Report written: 21 Apr 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0004-0026 at 13:15 on 2023-04-20 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.4% of the pad area, estimated 2.4 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 318 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 254 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0004-003; the manifest was only completed the following week (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.52% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0004-021

Asset: WELL-0004 (SW-23 Well 004, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 21 Feb 2026 08:00 · Finished: 17 Mar 2026 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 570 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0004-0172 on 2026-02-19 Report written: 18 Mar 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0004-0172 showed the wellhead at 18.7 °C with the air at 8.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0004-026

Asset: WELL-0004 (SW-23 Well 004, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 19 Jul 2026 08:00 · Finished: 28 Jul 2026 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 220 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0004-0192 on 2026-07-16 Report written: 30 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0004-0192 showed the wellhead at 46.3 °C with the air at 36.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 7 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.
